provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Fluency lines
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write straight lines neatly.
The pupils should be able to write with speed and control.
Introduction:
Last term we learned how to hold our pencils well.
Today we will practice writing straight lines.
Content:
We will write full lines from left to right.
We must keep our letters the same size.
We will write fast but not messy.
Practice on the board first.
Class activity:
Each child will write five straight lines in their notebook.
The teacher will walk around to help.
Evaluation questions:
Show me how to hold your pencil.
What should we remember when writing lines?
Can you write fast but still neat?
Summary:
Today we learned to write straight lines neatly and with control.

topics.title: Word families copy
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to copy word family lists.
The pupils should be able to check their letter joins.
Introduction:
We know some letters make sounds together.
Today we will write words that sound similar.
Content:
Word families are words with same endings.
For example cat, bat, rat all end with-at.
We write these words in our notebooks.
We must join letters well when writing.
Class activity:
Children will copy three word families.
They will trade books with a friend to check joins.
Evaluation questions:
What is a word family?
Show me how to join letters in 'bat'.
Find three words in the-at family.
Summary:
Today we copied word families and checked our letter joins.

topics.title: Sight words writing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write sight words from memory.
The pupils should be able to spell and write sight words together.
Introduction:
Some words we see all the time.
We can write these without sounding them out.
Content:
Sight words are common words we know by sight.
Examples are the, and, is, my.
We will practice writing these words.
First we say the letters then write them.
Class activity:
Teacher calls out sight words.
Children write them in their notebooks from memory.
Evaluation questions:
What is a sight word?
Write the word 'the' without looking.
How many letters are in the word 'and'?
Summary:
Today we practiced writing sight words from memory.

topics.title: Sentence writing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write their own sentences.
The pupils should be able to use capital letters and full stops.
Introduction:
We know how to write words now.
Today we will put words together to make sentences.
Content:
A sentence is a group of words that makes sense.
Every sentence must start with a big letter.
Every sentence must end with a full stop.
We will write about things we like.
Class activity:
Children will write two sentences about their favorite food.
They will circle the capital letters and full stops.
Evaluation questions:
What starts every sentence?
What ends every sentence?
Write a sentence about your pet.
Summary:
Today we learned to write sentences with capitals and full stops.

topics.title: Question sentences
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write and answer questions.
The pupils should be able to use question marks.
Introduction:
Sometimes we ask questions.
Questions need a special mark at the end.
Content:
A question asks something.
It ends with a question mark like this ?.
We will write questions about our friends.
We will also write answers to questions.
Class activity:
Children will write one question about their friend.
They will write an answer to their friend's question.
Evaluation questions:
What mark ends a question?
Write a question about the weather.
What is different about a question sentence?
Summary:
Today we learned to write questions with question marks.

topics.title: Little paragraph
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write three linked sentences.
The pupils should be able to write about their family.
Introduction:
We know how to write sentences.
Today we will write many sentences about one topic.
Content:
A paragraph is many sentences about one thing.
We will write three sentences about our family.
The sentences must connect together.
We will use capital letters and full stops.
Class activity:
Children will write three sentences about their family.
They will draw a picture to match their writing.
Evaluation questions:
What is a paragraph?
How many sentences will you write?
What must all your sentences be about?
Summary:
Today we wrote a little paragraph about our family.

topics.title: Number words to twenty
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write number words.
The pupils should be able to match digits and words.
Introduction:
We know numbers like 1 2 3.
Today we will learn to write number words.
Content:
Number words are how we say numbers.
One, two, three up to twenty.
We will write these words in our books.
We will match numbers to their words.
Class activity:
Children will write number words from 1 to 10.
They will play a matching game with number cards.
Evaluation questions:
How do you write the number 5?
Match the number 3 to its word.
What number word comes after seven?
Summary:
Today we learned to write number words to twenty.

topics.title: Dictation 1
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write words from dictation.
The pupils should be able to write one sentence from dictation.
Introduction:
Sometimes we need to write what we hear.
Today we will listen and write down words.
Content:
Dictation means writing what someone says.
We will write some simple words first.
Then we will write one short sentence.
We must listen carefully to all the sounds.
Class activity:
Teacher will say five simple words.
Children will write them in their notebooks.
Teacher will say one sentence for children to write.
Evaluation questions:
What is dictation?
Show me how you listen carefully.
Why is it important to listen during dictation?
Summary:
Today we practiced writing words and a sentence from dictation.

topics.title: Dictation 2
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write two sentences from dictation.
The pupils should be able to check their own work.
Introduction:
Last week we did dictation with words.
Today we will write two longer sentences.
Content:
Dictation helps us write what we hear.
We will write two sentences this time.
After writing we will check our work.
We will look for capital letters and full stops.
Class activity:
Children will write two sentences from teacher's dictation.
They will swap books with a partner to check work.
Evaluation questions:
How many sentences will you write today?
What should you check after writing?
What makes a good sentence?
Summary:
Today we wrote two sentences and checked our work.

topics.title: Revision and writing show
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write their best independent page.
The pupils should be able to participate in a writing award.
Introduction:
We have learned many writing skills.
Today we will show our best writing.
Content:
We will write our best page all by ourselves.
We will use all we learned this term.
Neat lines, good sentences, proper capitals.
We will have a writing show to celebrate.
Class activity:
Children will write their best page in their notebook.
The class will walk around to see everyone's writing.
Evaluation questions:
What writing skill are you proud of?
What makes good handwriting?
Show me your best writing.
Summary:
Today we showed our best writing and celebrated our progress.
